newsitem.title: USA: Lowrance sees profit in FY97.
newsitem.headline: Lowrance sees profit in FY97.

text.p: Lowrance Electronics Inc said Friday it continues to expect "meaningful growth and profitability" in fiscal 1997.
Earlier, Lowrance reported a net loss for the second quarter ended January 31 of $1,246,000 or $0.37 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $380,000 or $0.11.
The current backlog is approximately $21 million compared to approximately $13 million at the same time last year.
In fiscal 1996, Lowrance Electronics earned $0.52 a share.

"The second half of our fiscal year is typically the strongest selling season for our Lowrance and Eagle sonar product lines, and we expect this year to be no exception," Darrell Lowrance, president, said in a statement. "The company recently introduced six mid- and high-end sonar products that were available in very limited quantities in the second quarter, which restrained revenue and gross margin for the period, but are now in full production."
Based on orders in hand, the company expects sharply higher shipments of these products beginning in this quarter.

The year-ago second quarter included sales of certain older mid- and high-end sonar products whose production was discontinued last summer in anticipation of the launch of the new models, Lowrance said.

"In addition, demand for our new line of low cost, hand-held global positioning system (GPS) instruments has surpassed our expectations, and we've made great strides in the development of new distribution channels for these products," he added. "We expect sales of our GPS instruments, many of which were not in our product lineup a year ago, to make a significant incremental contribution to Lowrance's financial performance in the second half and to materially contribute to revenue growth for the remainder of the year."

Lowrance Electronics designs and manufactures sonar products and orbital satellite receivers, plotters and mapping systems, which are used primarily for sport fishing, hunting, recreational boating and other outdoor applications as well as in general aviation.
